text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The editorial said the government should not have made public the International Monetary Fund's advice to close down pyramid schemes, because of the alarm it caused to many Albanians for who rely on such schemes for their income.
- Two Albanian firms installing new telephone lines in the capital have sued an Italian partner for breach of contract.
- The appeals trial of a Briton sentenced to two years in jail for sexually abusing two Albanian minors is to be held on October 16.
- The opposition Democratic Alliance is to take a German politician to court for helping with the ruling party electoral campaign. If found guilty he could be sentenced to up to three years in jail.
- Local elections will serve as a test for a possible association agreement Albania hopes to sign with the European Union.
- Albania's supreme court of cassation ruled foreign observers monitoring elections must be at least 22 and Albanian observers 25 years old.
- Weaker demand for cash hard currency has strengthened the lek. The dollar fell to 106.3 leks from 107 leks on Tuesday.
- Albania's Science Academy is beset by financial woes, causing many scientists to seek work abroad.
- Portugal's soccer coach Artur Jorge is convinced his team will beat Albania in the group nine World Cup soccer qualifier in Tirana.
- Two Italian opposition parties have asked the government to use the army to stop the flow of illegal immigrants from neighbouring Albania.
- The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe has requested accreditation for 55 observers for Albania's local elections on October 20.
- Albania lost a great friend on the death of Lord Finsberg, British delegation honorary president in the Council of Europe, the paper said.
- The paper alleged that Albania's ruling party had illegally spent the government's 1996 budget of 99 billion leks in the first six months of the year on its election campaign.
